output.title: Design out the error that feeds itself
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the problem is usually not the last error. It is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

A useful question is: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? If invoice details are entered by hand and then reconciled by hand because the first entry was incomplete or misclassified, you do not have two separate problems. You have one loop.

The next step is to check whether the workflow is actually a fit for automation. Ask four things: is it repetitive, does it produce a measurable outcome, does it live in digital documents or SaaS tools, and do you have the authority to change the process? If the answer is no, AI is probably the wrong tool. Change the workflow first.

If the answer is yes, define one error-blocking control before anything else. That might be duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step. For money movement, human approval stays in place. The system should catch the mistake before it gets a chance to cycle back. Boring, but that is usually the point.

Then pilot one workflow with one control. Not the whole business, just the loop that keeps teaching itself the same mistake.
